# Exploratory follow-up of 13.11.2026 (course folder pro/followup-2026-11-12/results.md), chosen after the
# night run of 12.11 and three reviews. Not in the plan; decides no hypothesis. Bars and predictions below
# were written before the run. "Reduction" is the relative error reduction of the main report.
#
# Feature-sampling control inside the benchmark. The 10 datasets of size.toml at 4,000 training rows, seed 0,
# 5 folds. Check "all": every cascade forest tries all columns at each split (max_features = 1.0). Check
# "sqrt_copy": target_copy_xx with DF21's sqrt(m), the one reference that size.toml (check n4000) lacks.
# 5 x 10 x 5 + 10 x 5 = 300 tasks.
#
# Bars (10 datasets; "most" = at least 8):
# - F5 the noise penalty is about sampling: with all columns the reduction of target_noise_xx against base is
#   closer to zero than with sqrt(m) on most datasets, at layer 1 and at the chosen layer. Prediction: yes.
# - F6 products still do not help: with all columns residual_xx is not a clear win over base (median > 0 and
#   at least 8 of 10 better). Prediction: no clear win.
# - F7 all columns is not a better base: base with all columns beats base with sqrt(m) on most datasets.
#   Prediction: no (sqrt(m) is the usual choice for a reason). If F5 holds and F7 fails, the cost of added
#   columns is the price of the decorrelation that sqrt(m) buys.
datasets = ["parkinsons", "air_quality", "ccpp", "phishing", "bike_sharing", "bank_marketing", "adult",
            "credit_default", "california", "superconductivity"]
seeds = [0]
outer_folds = 5

[[check]]
name = "all"
methods = ["base", "target_xx", "residual_xx", "target_copy_xx", "target_noise_xx"]
cascade = { train_rows = 4000, max_features = 1.0 }

[[check]]
name = "sqrt_copy"
methods = ["target_copy_xx"]
cascade = { train_rows = 4000 }
